questions.q: A simple generator consists of a coil of wire forced to rotate about an axis in a magnetic field. What energy transformation does this generator perform?
options: It transforms electrical energy into mechanical kinetic energy
It transforms mechanical kinetic energy into electrical energy
It transforms chemical energy into electrical energy
It transforms electrical energy into heat energy
questions.explanation: A generator is a device that transforms mechanical kinetic energy into electrical energy - the exact reverse of a motor. The coil is forced to rotate in the magnetic field, the flux threading the coil changes, and Faraday's Law gives the induced emf across the ends of the coil.

questions.q: As the coil of a generator is forced to rotate about an axis in a magnetic field, what directly causes an emf to be induced across the ends of the wire of the coil?
options: The steady, unchanging strength of the magnetic field
The changing magnitude of the magnetic flux threading the area of the coil
A current supplied to the coil by the external circuit
The heat produced in the stator by the rotating rotor
questions.explanation: As the coil rotates, the magnitude of the magnetic flux threading the area of the coil changes, and this changing magnetic flux produces a changing emf across the ends of the wire, in accordance with Faraday's Law of Induction. The stationary parts are the stator, which provides the field; the rotating coil is the rotor.

questions.q: At the instant the magnetic flux threading the generator coil is at a maximum value, what is the magnitude of the induced emf?
options: Maximum, because the flux threading the coil is maximum at that instant
Zero, because the gradient of the flux-versus-time graph is zero at that instant
Half of its peak value, because the coil is halfway through a revolution
Maximum negative, because the flux is about to reverse
questions.explanation: When the flux threading the coil is at a maximum value the emf is zero, because the gradient of the flux-versus-time graph is zero - there is no change in flux at that instant. Conversely, when the flux threading the coil is zero the emf is at its maximum value, because the change in flux is then happening at a maximum rate.

questions.q: From memory, in terms of the graph of magnetic flux threading the coil versus time, explain why a generator's emf is zero when the flux is at a maximum and maximum when the flux is zero.
keyPoints: The emf is given by the negative of the gradient of the graph of magnetic flux threading the coil versus time (Faraday's Law) - not by the flux itself.
When the flux threading the coil is at a maximum value, the gradient of the flux-versus-time graph is zero, so there is no change in flux at that instant and the emf is zero.
When the flux threading the coil is zero, the flux-versus-time graph has its maximum gradient - the change in flux is happening at a maximum rate - so the emf is at a maximum value.
questions.explanation: The single most-missed mark in this topic: the emf tracks the rate of change of flux (the gradient of the flux-time graph), not the flux. Maximum flux gives zero emf; zero flux gives maximum emf, ninety degrees out of phase.

questions.q: How does an AC generator connect its rotating coil to the external circuit, and what is the nature of the output?
options: A split-ring commutator, giving a unidirectional output
Slip rings that rotate with the coil, giving an emf that varies sinusoidally as an alternating current
Two fixed terminals soldered directly to the coil, giving a steady direct current
A multi-part commutator, giving a smooth constant voltage
questions.explanation: An AC generator connects the coil to the external circuit by the use of slip rings, which rotate with the coil; brushes make contact with the slip rings and transfer the emf to the terminals. The emf across the ends of the coil varies sinusoidally with time, producing an alternating current (AC).

questions.q: What is the essential difference between a simple AC generator and a simple DC generator in the way the current is provided to the external circuit?
options: An AC generator's coil rotates while a DC generator's coil stays still
An AC generator uses slip rings, while a DC generator uses a split-ring commutator to connect the rotating coil to the terminals
An AC generator uses an electromagnet while a DC generator uses permanent magnets
An AC generator induces an emf by Faraday's Law while a DC generator does not
questions.explanation: The difference between an AC and a DC generator is in the way the current is provided to the external circuit: an AC generator uses slip rings, while a DC generator uses a split-ring commutator. When the emf of the coil changes direction, the brushes swap over the side of the coil they are connected to, causing the emf supplied to the external circuit to be in one direction only.

questions.q: From memory: explain how the split-ring commutator of a simple DC generator keeps the current supplied to the external circuit in one direction, and describe the shape of the output.
keyPoints: A DC generator uses a split-ring commutator to connect the rotating coil to the terminals; the coil itself still induces the same emf as in an AC generator.
When the emf of the coil changes direction, the brushes swap over the side of the coil they are connected to, so the emf supplied to the external circuit is in one direction only.

The output is a pulsating unidirectional DC (a rectified sine wave) that rises from zero to a maximum and back twice per revolution - not a steady, flat line; it can be made smoother by adding more coils on the armature with a multi-part commutator.
questions.explanation: Precision matters for the marks: the commutator reverses the external connection, not the emf in the coil. A simple single-coil DC generator gives pulsating DC, never a flat constant value.

questions.q: How can the output from a simple single-coil DC generator be made smoother?
options: By spinning the single coil at a much higher frequency
By replacing the split-ring commutator with slip rings
By including more coils set at regular angles on the armature, each connected to segments of a multi-part commutator, so the brushes contact the coil producing the greatest emf
By winding the coil onto a non-magnetic plastic core
questions.explanation: The output from a DC generator can be made smoother by including more coils set at regular angles on the armature. Each coil is connected to two segments of a multi-part commutator, and the brushes make contact only with the segments connected to the coil producing the greatest emf at a particular time - a two-coil generator uses a four-segment commutator.

questions.q: A rectangular generator coil of 200 turns and area 0.075 m^2 rotates in a uniform magnetic field of 0.66 T at 50 revolutions per second. Find the angular frequency and the peak emf of the sinusoidal output.
working: Peak emf is the peak of the sinusoid from Faraday's Law applied to \(\Phi = BA\cos\omega t\): \(\varepsilon_{\max} = NBA\omega\)
questions.explanation: NBA-omega is not on the formula sheet but is just the peak of the sinusoid you get by applying Faraday's Law to a flux of BA cos(omega t). With slip rings the terminals deliver this as a full AC sine wave; with a split-ring commutator the negative halves are flipped positive, giving pulsating DC of the same peak.

questions.q: A single rectangular loop measuring 0.25 m by 0.30 m sits in a perpendicular field of 0.66 T. The flux is swept from zero to its full value over 2.0 s. Find the magnitude of the average induced emf.
questions.explanation: This bare-mechanism version uses only formula-sheet maths: emf = N times the change in flux over the change in time gives the average emf over the sweep, whereas NBA-omega gives the peak of a sinusoid. Scale by N for a real multi-turn coil.
